findings.description: The policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the user full control over essentially every EC2, S3, Lambda and CloudWatch resource in the account. This violates least privilege and includes high-impact permissions such as s3:* (data exfiltration/deletion), lambda:* and iam-adjacent escalation paths, so any compromise of this principal is effectively account-wide.

A static IAM access key pair is created for svc_deploy, which also holds the wildcard policy above. Long-lived access keys do not expire, are not protected by MFA, and if leaked (e.g. via state, CI logs, or source control) grant persistent, non-expiring access to the full set of wildcard permissions.

This output deliberately surfaces the access key's secret material as a Terraform output. Outputs are persisted in the Terraform state file and echoed by plan/apply, so the credential is exposed to anyone with state access or console output, defeating the protection of the secret.
